{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the start of the round and set the design: one start at the nose end, two lines splitting around the body, and a flared tail. I drew it on the pad, so the whole table had one shared plan from the first minute. I also laid the start domino and traced stroke 1, the top line, which every other piece depends on. Before the push, the fish traced as fully connected, all 101 standing dominoes from the start.

Execution: I sketched the fish with gentle curves and no sharp corners, so it could be built as a single run. I built stroke 1 in several batches from the start domino out to the nose. After that I inspected the top line and the nose joint repeatedly to look for hidden gaps. Once the picture was connected, I kept my hands off it so I wouldn't knock anything over.

Collaboration: I split the work early. I asked for dominoes for the bin and assigned the bottom line so the top and bottom could be built in sequence. I thanked teammates as their pieces came together and stayed out of their way while they worked near the nose and tail, to avoid bumps.

Leadership: I picked the animal, set the plan, and named who would take which stroke in the first minute, so there was no debate or lost time. I then kept the table calm and focused on a connected fish rather than extra detail. I'm confident the fish design and the top-line trace were central to the result.", "my_share_percent": 35}
